title: fix: reserve API key budgets atomically instead of read-then-compare
author: davealan74
pr_body_excerpt:
- `checkBalance` compared a stale auth-time balance snapshot against the estimated cost; concurrent requests on one key all passed the same check and were billed in full at settlement, so the balance had no bound tied to the key's budget.
- Adds `atomicReserveApiKeyBalance`: one UPDATE that decrements and admits only if there's headroom, closing the race at admission instead of guarding settlement. A settlement-side guard doesn't work here: the wallet is debited before the key, so a rejected key UPDATE would throw after the wallet is already charged and skip the BYOP/community payouts that run later in the same try.
- `atomicDeductApiKeyBalance` → `atomicAdjustApiKeyBalance(delta)`: settlement now reconciles the actual billed price against what was reserved instead of charging on top of it, and a request that ends up unbilled refunds the reservation in full.
- Same reservation threaded through the realtime WebSocket route, which takes its own reservation via `checkBalance` but settles independently of the main `track.ts` path.
- Known residual: an uncaught crash between a successful reservation and settlement leaves the hold unreleased. No background reconciliation job exists for this today on the wallet side either, so out of scope here.

Fixes #12851

gist.headline: No more budget stampedes
gist.blurb: One API key budget, one orderly queue at the hive door. Concurrent generations now reserve their Pollen before heading out, then settle against the amount they actually used.
gist.summary: API key budgets now use an atomic reserve-at-admission update across HTTP, audio, proxy, and realtime WebSocket generation routes, with settlement reconciling actual cost against the reserved amount or refunding it when a request is unbilled.
gist.impact: Concurrent requests sharing one API key now stay within that key's configured budget instead of all passing the same stale balance check and being charged later.
gist.visual_concept: Depict API-key budget control as a cozy hive gate with a small set of pollen jars being reserved one at a time before bees enter generation tunnels. Polli acts as the careful keeper with a tiny accountant visor and clipboard, while a friendly CRT monitor robot watches a realtime WebSocket cable; code-plants and flowers reinforce that orderly resource sharing helps the garden grow.
